analysis: Only two base_text excerpts of coordinator/api/dispatch.go were supplied (start lines 675 and 1417). No patch hunks or head-side text were included, so I could not identify what the PR changes. I examined the base-side dispatch logic: failure classification (isGenuinePreContentFault, classifyExhaustedStatus, resolveDominantExhaustedStatus), terminal client error latching, queue path (dispatchPrimary), E2E encryption of the request to the provider public key (e2e.ParsePublicKey, GenerateSessionKeys, e2e.Encrypt) with cache sealing via bodyForCacheAttempt/PrepareCacheAttempt, and failover/stop policy (shouldStopFailover, latchDeterministicLoser). In the queued path, the code fails closed when the provider public key is empty or invalid and when encryption fails (T-008, T-003). I found no authorization bypass, plaintext leakage, or billing regression in the supplied text; refunds and RemovePending run on failure paths. Cache scoping uses coordinator-derived d.cachePlan, consistent with T-041 account scoping. Final-dispatch App Attest authorization (T-053/TB-011) is not visible in these excerpts, so the queue-assigned path's reliance on registry-level checks could not be confirmed. Coverage limitation: without the diff, the security effect of the change is unassessed, so another pass with the actual patch hunks is warranted.
